title: nil, true, false, and Truthiness
subtopics: Why values such as 0 and empty strings are truthy
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of nil, true, false, and truthiness in a Ruby program and name the key rule involved.
Apply nil, true, false, and truthiness in a small example and predict its result before running it.
Identify one boundary or failure case related to why values such as 0 and empty strings are truthy and verify the intended behavior.

content.intro: Learn nil, true, false, and Truthiness through a visual model, a minimal Ruby example, and a practical check.
content.why_it_matters: Understanding nil, true, false, and truthiness helps you write code that is easier to explain, test, and maintain. It also helps separate Ruby language guarantees from runtime assumptions, dependency behavior, and application-specific rules.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: nil, true, false, and Truthiness helps you reason about boolean values. In Ruby, prefer a small example whose inputs and expected result are easy to explain. This lesson connects the syllabus topic to practical code and highlights where assumptions or edge cases matter.

content_blocks.title: How to think about it
content_blocks.text: Begin by identifying the key rule: Boolean values. Then connect it to The meaning of nil. The remaining syllabus points—Truthy and falsy values, Why values such as 0 and empty strings are truthy—are useful checks before applying this in a larger project.
